scope: read-only rowid-range full-snapshot design assessment; no implementation, SQL execution, benchmark or original acceptance credit
conclusion: Rowid ranges eliminate the two concrete path-IN flaws and are a plausible narrow prototype for successful-result/fail-closed equivalence. Exact first-error ordering is not preserved by any simple deferred scheme and must not be claimed. No performance adoption or execution authorization is granted by this review.

observed_write_contract.fact: files uses plain INSERT with no explicit rowid, no REPLACE.
literal_index uses INSERT OR IGNORE without explicit rowid. Ignored conflicts do not create another base row.
Complete per-file function has no DELETE of either table; REPLACE statements target other fact tables.
Chunk delete triggers remove chunk identity/document_manifest only.
literal FK references files; no reverse cascade from replaced symbol/edge rows to these bases. Files triggers modify file_paths_fts only. Neither base declares a user rowid alias nor WITHOUT ROWID.
One transaction owns complete write_fn; error aborts staging and removes temp file before publication.

source_only_algorithm.before: Read coalesce(max(rowid),0) separately for files and literal_index immediately before each nonempty <=256-file window.
source_only_algorithm.body: Original file iteration and every base/leaf binder remain in order; set both internal snapshot flags true rather than calling public deferred helper that disables leaf batching. No per-row files/literal mirror in this body.
source_only_algorithm.after: Read current maxima if closed bounds desired, then two fixed INSERT INTO ... SELECT ... WHERE rowid > ? AND rowid <= ? statements, optionally explicit ORDER BY rowid for documented ascending mirror order.
source_only_algorithm.survivors: Original successful insert set for each base is exactly the rowid interval under monotonicity assumptions. Ignored duplicate literal ids produce no new row, even across windows; earlier winner never gets mirrored again.
source_only_algorithm.cross_file_attribution: The actually stored literal row is selected by rowid independently of literal.file_path, so a later literal referencing an earlier file is included.
source_only_algorithm.cost: With before+after reads: four scalar SELECTs plus two mirror statements per window. Base row B-tree persists while explicit secondary indexes are dropped; no path predicate over all older literals. Actual query plan and measured advantage remain unverified.
source_only_algorithm.space: Two/four i64 markers plus existing slice references; no cross-file leaf payload collection.

official_sources.claim: Implicit rowid is max+1, starting1 when empty. Without deletions and without ever using signed-i64 maximum, generated rowids increase. At max i64 SQLite can select unused positive rowids randomly.
rowid is the row-table B-tree access key; VACUUM may change implicit rowids.

monotonicity_limits.current_path: No DELETE/UPDATE-rowid/VACUUM of these two bases inside observed window, no concurrent writer on transaction-owned connection, no external callback within per-file contents. Other table REPLACE does not violate these two-base monotonicity.
monotonicity_limits.freshness_caution: build_rebuild_staging cleanup at80-83 ignores remove errors; SnapshotWriteTxn::new is public and accepts an arbitrary connection. Therefore fresh-empty cannot be elevated to a universally enforced API invariant. High-water markers work on ordinary preexisting rows too, but need overflow-safe fallback.
monotonicity_limits.preserve_accepted_inputs: If exposed through same public SnapshotWriteTxn seam, do not introduce a novel refusal for unusual preexisting rowids. Bound potential new base insert counts before window using checked arithmetic; if max+count can exceed i64 maximum, retain original per-row mirrors for that window. This is a proposed compatibility fallback, not existing implementation.
monotonicity_limits.future_hooks: Any new base DELETE/REPLACE, explicit rowid, VACUUM, extra statement/callback or trigger mutating these bases invalidates the proof. Keep helper private/crate-private and document/update tests at this seam.

interface_reuse.existing_public_helper: insert_files_literal_fts_batch accepts paths and cannot represent a rowid range; do not broaden it into arbitrary SQL or change incremental callers.
interface_reuse.minimal_internal_change: Add a snapshot-only private/crate-private typed marker/range helper with literal fixed table SQL and i64 binds, reuse execute_cached and existing per-file internal body. SnapshotWriteTxn public signature and general IndexDb APIs remain unchanged.

failure_and_observation.unavoidable_order_change: An FTS I/O/SQLITE_FULL/tokenizer/constraint failure formerly after file A now follows base/leaf writes of files A..window-end. Another error in a later base/identity statement may win instead. At most the transaction abort/publication guarantee is preserved; exact earliest error text/order is not equivalent.
failure_and_observation.same_connection_visibility: No current production callback observes half-populated files/literal FTS inside write_file_data. A caller sees only return after all windows flush. A future hook or direct SQL observer inside that seam would be a new concern.
failure_and_observation.last_insert_rowid: Every retained chunks mirror still reads immediately after its own chunks insert. Delayed files/literal inserts must not make any later identity logic rely on an earlier last_insert_rowid; existing inspected function's captures remain local.
failure_and_observation.publication: Flush each window and final remainder before route/config/metadata/baseline; retain original transaction, same error propagation and no swap on any failure.

minimal_falsifiers_not_executed: Full actual staging adapter with dropped explicit indexes: EXPLAIN rowid SELECTs must show rowid range access rather than growing table scans.
0/1/255/256/257 files and zero/many literals; nonadjacent duplicate literal ids; late literal referencing a prior window file; cross-file uid/id collisions and duplicate file failures.
Compare all canonical/identity rows and all FTS rowid/content/MATCH results, plus chunks/file_paths mirrors, after reopen. Include a transaction rollback/error case before and during flush.
An arbitrary prepopulated seam connection with high/maximum rowid and planned insert-count overflow must retain original behavior through fallback or the seam must demonstrably be inaccessible there.
Small deterministic AB/BA under same staging adapter and fixed source before any formal performance study. Existing G2 stage timing does not show the proposed implementation is fast.
